comparator.name: Ancient Studies
comparator.institution: University of Amsterdam and Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam
comparator.sourceNotes: The joint degree combines interdisciplinary Ancient Studies with one required specialisation. This example selects Ancient History, the broad historical direction and first-listed specialisation in the adopted regulations, before considering UCR. It includes Classical Mythology and Seminar Ancient History as the two orientation choices, five named specialisation courses, 30 EC open space and a 12 EC thesis including the thesis colloquium. All three years total 60 EC.

components.name: Objects in Context: An Interdisciplinary Perspective on the Ancient World
components.note: The Academic Literacy Test, ACASA orientation and tutoring support carry no credits. Writing support is provided when the diagnostic test indicates it is needed.

components.name: The Classical Canon 1: The Heritage of Antiquity
A Cultural History of the Ancient World 1: The Near East and the Greek World
A Cultural History of the Ancient World 2: The Hellenistic World, Italy and Rome
Seminar Ancient History
components.note: This orientation seminar follows the two first-year cultural-history surveys and prepares for Ancient History. Seminar participation is compulsory.

components.name: Cultural Contact: Mediterranean Connections
components.note: Entry requires both first-year Cultural History of the Ancient World courses, or equivalent introductory study.

components.name: ACASA excursion
components.note: Students prepare and carry out an interdisciplinary excursion research project. Practical exercises require at least 85% attendance under the programme regulations.

components.name: Past and Present: Critical Approaches to Antiquity and Archaeological Heritage
The Classical Canon 2: The Sociology of Cultural Selection
History and Culture of the Ancient Near East
The Decline and Fall of Rome
Politics and International Relations in Antiquity
Free-choice electives
components.note: The 30 EC elective period may include a minor, approved study abroad or a placement of up to 12 EC. Normally no more than 12 EC may be introductory, and at least 24 EC must be outside the programme. Approved exceptions apply to specified minors and language sequences.

components.name: In Search of the Masses of Antiquity
Bachelor's Thesis Ancient Studies
components.note: The 12 EC thesis includes the thesis colloquium. Students must pass all first- and second-year courses before starting. They conduct individual interdisciplinary research under supervision.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The generic merged target includes Dutch and English delivery. The English Ancient Studies track represents its international academic identity. Ancient History is the broad historical specialisation rather than a specific language or material-method route and is also first in Article 10.2 and the specialisation table. The selection precedes UCR implementation.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest option implements a balanced ancient material, textual and intellectual core. Archaeology and public memory and political history and reception are coherent target-supported priorities, with substantive curricular consequences. Each pair passes the thirty-EC floor. Language-specific directions remain acknowledged limitations rather than weak separate programmes. Three is the maximum.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both interpret material objects as evidence of past societies and develop archaeological documentation and inference.
Both investigate contested heritage, ownership and public narratives; UCR focuses on African art, colonial collections and restitution rather than the UNESCO framework.
Both examine later cultural uses and transformations of classical heritage; UCR concentrates on Renaissance visual culture and its wider connections.
Both use material evidence to study ancient Greek communities; the external survey also covers the Near East and a longer chronology.
Both examine cultural selection and the institutions and narratives that make works canonical; UCR focuses on modern art and museums.
Both examine participation, social groups and exclusion in ancient political life using textual and material evidence; UCR concentrates on Athens.
Both examine disciplinary methods, knowledge and interpretation in the humanities; UCR focuses on art history.
Both investigate empire, political power and decline with historical sources; UCR compares Rome with other ancient and later empires.
Both use theories of interstate relations to interpret political conflict; UCR uses modern cases while the external course works directly from ancient evidence.
Both develop interpretation of ancient philosophical arguments; UCR extends into later and contemporary philosophy.
Both interpret influential ancient literary works and their cultural significance; UCR also compares later works.
Both study Greek and Roman myth, its transmission and cultural interpretation; UCR compares further traditions.
Both develop creative writing, revision and critical justification of forms for a wider audience; UCR is not restricted to classical reception.

notes.text: The joint UvA–VU degree combines ancient textual and material sources with a required specialisation, excursion and thesis. This example follows Ancient History. UCR offers related study in archaeology, myth, philosophy, heritage and historical interpretation, but does not reproduce the full ancient-history sequence or provide Greek, Latin or Akkadian language sequences.

audience.programmeDescription: Ancient Studies is a joint UvA–VU degree combining the history, texts, objects and ideas of the ancient Mediterranean and Near East. Students study cultural interaction and the later uses of antiquity, then complete a specialisation and interdisciplinary thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR options connect archaeology, ancient democracy, literature, myth and philosophy with historical and cultural interpretation. The joint degree offers a more sustained ancient-world curriculum, a required specialisation and an excursion. This comparison uses its English-taught Ancient History route.
